statuses.title: per-group adaptive clip sync reduces group counts positionally
statuses.note: Fix commit 23521ab6 (#888). packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_distributed.py:64-71 now derives the collective schedule from the replicated schema: `current_pg = state._current_clipping_norm; group_names = sorted(current_pg.values)` and reduces `state._num_clipped[gname]` in that order, so the i-th all_reduce carries the same group on every rank regardless of dict insertion order. All three construction sites named in the OPQ entry were canonicalised too: `_empty_num_clipped()` -> `dict.fromkeys(sorted(initial_clipping_norm.values), 0.0)` (_adaptive.py:396), the stats path builds `{gname: stats.num_clipped[gname] for gname in sorted(current_pg.values)}` (_adaptive.py:539-551), and the engine's `_compute_clipping_stats` / `clipped_grad` empty paths sort as well (engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:412,495,513 and _clipped_grad.py:268). Traced the noise-fold index: the single-process per-group path folds `(ADAPTIVE_CLIPPING_STREAM_FOLD, state._step, i)` on the pre-increment step (_adaptive.py:559,592) and the sync folds `step_for_noise = max(0, state._step - 1)` on the post-increment state (_distributed.py:76-82), so both reach the same integer. `new_state._current_clipping_norm = state._next_clipping_norm` on both the empty and non-empty paths, so the schema is identical on an empty rank. No KeyError risk: `per_group()` drops unmatched patterns from `values` (engine/clipping/_per_group.py:180-185), so every key in `values` has at least one leaf. Ran the 2-rank gloo lane: packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py 6 passed, including test_per_group_adaptive_clipping_one_rank_empty_syncs, which now all_gathers the resulting thresholds and asserts rank agreement. Sibling scan for the same positional-reduce pattern found none left (engine `_gather_aux_fields` iterates the registered aux schema; `_sync_clipping_rate` issues a fixed two-collective schedule).

statuses.title: AdaClip accounting accepts invalid parameters on construction and deserialization
statuses.note: Fix commit 2ecc00a8 (#859). `AdaClip.__post_init__` exists at packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/mechanisms/_adaclip.py:40-63 and `Gaussian.__post_init__` at mechanisms/_gaussian.py:23-31. Reproduced every value named in OPQ-310 and all are now rejected on direct construction AND through the real `from_state_dict` codec path: num_groups=0 / -1 / 2.5, fraction_noise_std=-0.05, expected_batch_size=-250.0 and 0.0 all raise ConfigurationError; a valid num_groups=4 snapshot round-trips and still reports enm 1.09577. Gaussian(-1.0) is rejected while Gaussian(0.0) stays valid. CAVEAT (filed as a finding): `__post_init__` guards only the `<= 0` half of the range. `expected_batch_size=inf` and `fraction_noise_std=inf` load from a tampered snapshot and reproduce the exact symptom the fix was written to prevent - effective_noise_multiplier collapses to the bare 1.1 and poisson(...,0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5) reports 0.1422978, identical to `gaussian(1.1)` and to the 0.14229 OPQ-310 measured for num_groups=0. `inner` is also unvalidated in __post_init__ (the factory validates it), so a foreign inner makes `effective_noise_multiplier` fall through its `match` and return None against a `-> float` annotation; that direction is conservative in epsilon (measured 6.038 vs 1.515) and no shipped path consumes the None.

statuses.title: samplers seed numpy directly from the caller's key (no namespaced stream root)
statuses.note: Fix commit dd65957d (#884), DP-SGD scope (the dpftrl samplers in the same OPQ entry belong to the dpftrl reviewer). `POISSON_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpsgd.poisson"` (sampling/_poisson.py:34) and `K_OUT_OF_T_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpsgd.k_out_of_t"` (sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:26) are folded at construction (_poisson.py:97 `fold_in(key, POISSON_STREAM_FOLD)`; _k_out_of_t.py:55 `fold_in(key, K_OUT_OF_T_STREAM_FOLD, allocation)`), and the per-block derivation is `fold_in(self._stream_key, block)` (_k_out_of_t.py:129) - the RandomAllocation bare-integer fold the OPQ entry called out is gone with that class. Verified by execution: the Poisson stream no longer matches `np.random.default_rng(key.seed)`; neither sampler root lands in the caller-reachable set {key.seed} u split(key,16) u {fold_in(key,i) for i in -63..511}; block/total/Poisson built from one key(42) all produce different batch sequences. State-dict compatibility is handled by storing the post-fold stream key and restoring with `_from_stream_key` (test_poisson_state_dict.py::test_pre_domain_snapshot_uses_saved_seed_without_folding pins that a pre-#884 Poisson snapshot still replays its original stream, which is correct because pre-#884 Poisson seeded from the raw key). Tags are registered in docs/reference/rng.md:222-223.

statuses.title: accounting rejects sample_rate=1.0 that the runtime PoissonSampler supports
statuses.note: Fix commit 280e4969 (#853). `Poisson.__post_init__` now validates `not 0 < sample_rate <= 1` (accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:49) and `pld()` short-circuits `sample_rate == 1.0` by delegating to `self.inner.pld(...)` (:126-135). Verified numerically: `poisson(gaussian(1.1), 1.0) * 1000` gives epsilon 534.8979126040266 at delta=1e-5, bit-identical to `gaussian(1.1) * 1000`; the AdaClip inner path matches its unamplified counterpart to full precision (79.39286932042074 both ways); a q=1.0 process state-dicts and reloads. The truncated combination is still rejected with an explanatory ConfigurationError (:58-66). Runtime and accounting ranges now agree - the sampler validates `0 < sample_rate <= 1` (sampling/_poisson.py:~120) and docs/user-guide/sampling.md:42-45 and :76 both publish `(0, 1]` with the `sample_rate < 1` caveat for truncated Poisson.

statuses.title: O(G^2) random-allocation epoch transform rebuilt on every distinct step count
statuses.note: Resolved by two commits acting together. 87404a1b (#894) deleted horizon prefix accounting, so `KOutOfT` no longer exposes `pld_at(n)` - `pld()` computes the whole declared horizon once (accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_k_out_of_t.py:87-118) and `grep -rn 'pld_at|per_step'` over source and docs now returns nothing. 20dd47aa (#881) added the `epoch_pld` lru_cache (opaque-accounting/.../core/_random_allocation_cache.py:29-46) keyed on (nm, t, k, config). The OPQ-313 failure scenario is gone: measured k=8,t=512 - first `epsilon_at(1e-5)` 16.68 s, the second 0.01 s, and a structurally identical fresh `KOutOfT` instance also 0.01 s, so a trainer querying at every log boundary with a fixed delta pays once. CAVEAT (filed as a finding): the memoisation that the issue asked for is inert. `DpProcess.epsilon_at` rewrites `mc_resolution` to `delta/2` before calling `pld()` (opaque-accounting/.../core/_base.py:209-227), and that Monte-Carlo-only field is part of the `DiscretizationConfig` the lru_cache hashes, even though `random_allocation_gaussian_pld` never reads it. Measured `epoch_pld.cache_info()` after eps(1e-5) x2, eps(1e-6) and delta_at(3.0): hits=0, misses=3, with 16.2-16.7 s paid on each of the three misses.

statuses.title: dpsgd_acc.adaclip's num_groups parameter is documented nowhere
statuses.note: `num_groups` is now in both published signatures - docs/reference/accounting.md:312 `adaclip(inner, *, fraction_noise_std, expected_batch_size, num_groups=1) -> DpProcess` with a bullet at :321-323 explaining it is the number of independent noisy quantile queries, and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:179-185 with the same instruction. docs/user-guide/clipping.md:481-495 closes the loop the OPQ entry asked for: the 'Adaptive per-group clipping' section now tells the reader to pass `num_groups=pg.num_groups` and ships the runnable recipe. Verified `PerGroup.num_groups` exists and returns 2 for `per_group(params, self_attn=1.0, mlp=2.0)`, so the documented expression works. The accounting model matches the runtime: _adaptive.py:559 and :592 release one independently-noised rate per group per step, and AdaClip composes K quantile releases (mechanisms/_adaclip.py:79 via `adaclip_sensitivity(nm, sigma_b, num_groups)`, :125-126 for the generic branch).

findings.title: dpsgd_acc.poisson() lost its inner-mechanism guard and now silently amplifies already-amplified and whole-horizon processes
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (feat(accounting): generalize Poisson PLD amplification, #850) widened `_Inner` from `Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` to `DpProcess` and deleted the factory's `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate(): pass; case _: raise` guard that existed at the audit baseline. `Poisson.__post_init__` now only checks `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (:40), and `pld()` falls through to `_native.poisson_pld(self.inner.pld(...), self.sample_rate)` (:162) for anything non-truncated. The generic PLD-subsampling transform is sound for the model it implements (subsample the dataset once, then run the inner mechanism), but that is not what any Opaque runtime does, and the API offers no signal that the composed expression has left the DP-SGD model. Only the truncated branch kept a type guard (:91-98); the DP-FTRL sibling `dpftrl_acc.poisson` still restricts its inner to `MfGaussian` (packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../amplification/_poisson.py:279).
findings.failure_scenario: A user who already holds a per-step process and re-applies the amplification factory - `step = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), 0.01)` then `dpsgd_acc.poisson(step, 0.01) * 1000` - gets epsilon 0.00984 at delta=1e-5 where the correct DP-SGD figure is 1.51544, a 154x understatement, with no error and no warning. At the audit baseline that expression raised `TypeError: poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got Poisson`. Wrapping a whole-horizon process is equally silent: `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.1)` reports 0.10865 against the 0.97034 the horizon process reports on its own, and no Opaque sampler realises 'Poisson-subsample the dataset, then run k-out-of-t on the subsample'.
evidence: git show 3b22a6af -- packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py shows `-_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` / `+_Inner = DpProcess` and the removal of the factory guard.

git show 4b13d82:packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:170-175 contains the removed `case _: raise TypeError('poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner ...')`.

Executed on the current tree with a build of the current Rust extension: single = poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01); (single*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.5154423566628403; (poisson(single, 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009836885508304796.
Executed: kt = k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'); kt.epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.970343695110472; poisson(kt, 0.1).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.10865088995647369.
The Gaussian path itself is unchanged and correct - cross-validated against dp_accounting (connect-dots, disc 1e-4) at four (nm,q,T) points, Opaque conservative by 7e-5 to 6.7e-4.
findings.fix_sketch: Restore a guard in `Poisson.__post_init__` that rejects inner processes which are themselves participation models or compositions: `DpHorizonProcess` (KOutOfT, BMinSep, BallsInBins, CyclicPoisson), `Poisson`/`ParallelPoisson`, and the composition wrappers `Composed`/`Repeated`. Keep the generalisation for genuine single-release mechanisms, and say in the error which construction the user probably meant (`poisson(gaussian(nm), q) * n_steps`).

findings.title: adaclip is priced with train_batch_size under sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', whose expected batch size is dataset_size*k/t
findings.claim: `_build_mechanism` wraps the base Gaussian in `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(..., expected_batch_size=expected_batch_size, num_groups=num_groups)` (:4475-4479) before it branches on `a.sampling_mode`, and `expected_batch_size = a.train_batch_size` (:1472). That is the correct expectation only for Poisson sampling, where `sample_rate = train_batch_size / dataset_size`. Under `sampling_mode='k_out_of_t'` the sampler's own expectation is `num_samples * k / t` (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:114-116), and `t = total_steps ~ num_train_epochs * ceil(dataset_size/train_batch_size)` (_dp_trainer.py:4758-4767), so the two agree only when the user happens to set `k == num_train_epochs`. Nothing derives, constrains or warns about `k`: `_training_arguments.py:1311-1327` checks only that `k` and `allocation` are present and that `allocation` is 'block' or 'total'. This coupling used to be structural - at the audit baseline the equivalent parameter was `num_bins = expected_steps_per_epoch`, computed from `train_batch_size` (git show 4b13d82:.../_dp_trainer.py:4264-4277), so `dataset_size/num_bins ~= train_batch_size` by construction. fc44ec8d (#761) replaced the derived `num_bins` with a free user-supplied `k` and did not re-establish the link.
findings.failure_scenario: dataset_size=10000, per_device_train_batch_size=32, num_train_epochs=3 (so total_steps=900), clipping_mode='adaptive', sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', sampling_kwargs={'k': 1, 'allocation': 'block'}. TrainingArguments accepts this with no warning (verified). The sampler yields batches averaging 10000*1/900 = 11.1 examples, and `_adaptive.py:592-600` noises the realised rate `num_clipped/batch_size` with `fraction_noise_std`, i.e. an absolute count noise of about 11.1*0.05. The accountant is handed expected_batch_size=32, i.e. sigma_b = 32*0.05. At nm=1.0 the reported whole-horizon epsilon is 0.16890 while the value at the true expected batch size is 0.45493 - a 2.7x understatement. The direction is dangerous whenever k < num_train_epochs and conservative when k > num_train_epochs.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1472 `expected_batch_size = a.train_batch_size` and :4478 `expected_batch_size=expected_batch_size` inside the `clipping_mode == 'adaptive'` wrapper, which is applied before the `if a.sampling_mode == 'k_out_of_t':` branch at :4494.
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:114-116 `return self._num_samples * self.k / self.t`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:1311-1336 - the only k_out_of_t validation is presence of 'k'/'allocation' plus the allocation literal; :1284-1292 resolves adaptive to fixed only for DP-FTRL mechanisms, so gaussian + k_out_of_t + adaptive is permitted.

Executed: TrainingArguments(per_device_train_batch_size=32, num_train_epochs=3, privacy_target_epsilon=3.0, clipping_mode='adaptive', sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', sampling_kwargs={'k':1,'allocation':'block'}) is accepted with clipping_mode still 'adaptive' and zero warnings.

Executed: k_out_of_t(adaclip(gaussian(1.0), expected_batch_size=32), k=1, t=900, allocation='block').epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.16890 vs the same with expected_batch_size=10000/900=11.11 -> 0.45493 (effective_noise_multiplier 0.954480 vs 0.743294).
git show 4b13d82:.../_dp_trainer.py:1472,4264-4277 shows the pre-delta `num_bins=expected_steps_per_epoch` coupling that fc44ec8d removed.
findings.fix_sketch: Compute the accounting expected batch size from the sampling model rather than from `train_batch_size`: for `sampling_mode='k_out_of_t'` pass `dataset_size * k / n_steps` into `dpsgd_acc.adaclip` (and use it for `normalize_by` too, so the gradient scale matches the batches actually drawn). Alternatively derive `k` from `num_train_epochs` and reject an explicit `k` that contradicts it, restoring the pre-#761 structural coupling. Either way add a TrainingArguments check that `dataset_size * k / total_steps` is within a tolerance of `train_batch_size`, or a loud warning naming both values.

findings.title: the #881 random-allocation memoisation never serves a hit because epsilon_at folds a Monte-Carlo-only field into its cache key
findings.claim: `epoch_pld` is an `lru_cache` keyed on `(noise_multiplier, t, k, config)` where `config` is the whole frozen `DiscretizationConfig`, including `mc_resolution` and `mc_failure_probability`. `DpProcess.epsilon_at` overwrites `mc_resolution` with `min(configured, delta/2.0)` before calling `pld()` (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:209-227), and `delta_at` does not, so every distinct delta and every switch between the two entry points produces a distinct cache key. The underlying transform is deterministic and reads only `discretization`, `max_grid_size` and `tail_mass_truncation` (packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:164-224) - no Monte-Carlo field reaches it. The per-process `pld_cache` already covers the repeated-identical-query case, so `epoch_pld` contributes nothing through any public entry point. The package's own regression test calls `process.pld(**_CFG)` directly rather than `epsilon_at`, so it cannot observe this (packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_k_out_of_t_cache.py:35-39).
findings.failure_scenario: A user builds an epsilon-vs-delta curve, or simply calls `epsilon_at(1e-5)` and then `delta_at(target)`, on a k-out-of-t or balls-in-bins/identity process. Each new delta re-pays the full O(G^2) geometric-grid transform. Measured at k=8, t=512 with default discretization: 16.68 s for eps(1e-5), 0.01 s for the repeat, then 16.22 s for eps(1e-6) and 16.30 s for delta_at(3.0), with `epoch_pld.cache_info()` reporting hits=0, misses=3 throughout.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:29-35 - `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8) def epoch_pld(noise_multiplier, t, k, config)`.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:209-227 - `effective_resolution = min(configured_resolution, delta / 2.0)` passed as `mc_resolution` into `self.pld(...)`.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:164-224 - the transform reads config.discretization / max_grid_size / tail_mass_truncation only.

Executed after clear_random_allocation_caches() + KOutOfT.pld.cache_clear(): eps(1e-5)=1.98192 in 16.68s (misses=1), eps(1e-5) repeat 0.01s (misses=1, hits=0), eps(1e-6)=2.29745 in 16.22s (misses=2, hits=0), delta_at(3.0)=6.67e-09 in 16.30s (misses=3, hits=0), then a structurally identical fresh KOutOfT instance at 1e-5 in 0.01s with misses still 3 and hits still 0 (served by pld_cache, not by epoch_pld).
packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_k_out_of_t_cache.py:35-39 asserts misses==1 across two `process.pld(**_CFG)` calls, which the per-process pld_cache satisfies on its own.
findings.fix_sketch: Key `epoch_pld` on only the fields the transform reads - e.g. `(noise_multiplier, t, k, config.discretization, config.log_x_mass_truncation_bound, config.max_grid_size, config.max_conv_grid)` - or give `DiscretizationConfig` a `deterministic_key()` projection that drops `mc_resolution` / `mc_failure_probability` and hash that. Then retarget the regression test at `epsilon_at` with two different deltas and assert `epoch_pld.cache_info().hits >= 1`.

findings.title: AdaClip.__post_init__ guards only the non-positive half of its range, so expected_batch_size=inf still prices the quantile release as free
findings.claim: The #859 validation added to close OPQ-310 checks `fraction_noise_std <= 0`, `expected_batch_size <= 0` and `num_groups < 1 or != int(...)`. None of those comparisons is true for `+inf`, so a deserialized `AdaClip` with `expected_batch_size=inf` or `fraction_noise_std=inf` is accepted, `sigma_b` becomes infinite, the `K/(4*sigma_b^2)` term in `adaclip_sensitivity` vanishes, and `effective_noise_multiplier` collapses to the bare inner multiplier. That is the same 'prices adaptive clipping as free' outcome, in the same threat model (the generic `DpProcess` codec rebuilding with `cls(**kwargs)` from a corrupted or hand-edited checkpoint), that the comment at :41-44 says the validation exists to prevent. `inner` is also left unvalidated in `__post_init__` while the factory validates it (:164-173), so a foreign inner makes the `match` in `effective_noise_multiplier` (:74-80) fall through and return `None` from a `-> float` property.
findings.failure_scenario: A checkpoint's accountant JSON is edited or corrupted so `expected_batch_size` reads `Infinity`. `from_state_dict` rebuilds the AdaClip without error and `poisson(adaclip_process, 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5)` reports 0.1422978 - bit-identical to the unamplified-quantile `poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01)` figure, and matching to five digits the 0.14229 the original OPQ-310 report measured for `num_groups=0`. The run's adaptive-clipping quantile releases are then unaccounted. NaN in either field fails closed further downstream (ValueError from the native PLD), so +inf is the surviving fail-open value.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/mechanisms/_adaclip.py:41-44 - 'Validate here (not only in adaclip()) so direct construction and deserialization ... cannot produce an instance that prices the quantile release as free (e.g. num_groups=0).'
Same file :45-56 - the only bounds are `self.fraction_noise_std <= 0` and `self.expected_batch_size <= 0`.

Executed through the real codec (`state_dict(adaclip(gaussian(1.1), expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=4))`, field replaced, `from_state_dict`): expected_batch_size=inf -> ACCEPTED, effective_noise_multiplier=1.1, poisson(...,0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.1422977567766371; fraction_noise_std=inf -> identical result; the untampered process reports 0.14418327866598055 and `poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01)` reports 0.1422977567766371.

Executed: AdaClip(inner=poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01), ...) constructs without error and `effective_noise_multiplier` returns None; its pld() takes the generic `case _` branch and is conservative (6.038 vs 1.515 over 1000 steps), and no shipped path consumes the None.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the bounds to require finiteness: `if not math.isfinite(self.fraction_noise_std) or self.fraction_noise_std <= 0` and the same for `expected_batch_size`; do the same for `Gaussian.noise_multiplier` in mechanisms/_gaussian.py:28. Add an `isinstance(self.inner, (Gaussian, NonPrivate))` check to `AdaClip.__post_init__` so the dataclass and the factory agree, and give `effective_noise_multiplier` an explicit `case _: raise` instead of an implicit None.

findings.title: docs still name the removed random_allocation accounting factory
findings.claim: fc44ec8d (#761) deleted `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.random_allocation` and its module, folding the scheme into `k_out_of_t(..., allocation='block')`. The Monte-Carlo note in the accounting user guide still lists it as a live factory: 'Balls-in-Bins with identity_strategy(), and `random_allocation` and `k_out_of_t`, use deterministic transforms.' Verified the name is gone: `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__ == ['adaclip', 'gaussian', 'k_out_of_t', 'parallel_poisson', 'poisson']`. This is the same defect class as OPQ-357 (docs naming factories that do not exist), which the #843/#844 doc sweeps were closed for; the sweeps predate or missed this line.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader following the deterministic-vs-Monte-Carlo guidance writes `dpsgd_acc.random_allocation(...)` and gets an AttributeError. Loud rather than silently wrong, but it re-opens the drift that the closed documentation sweep was meant to eliminate, and it is the only surviving reference to the removed factory outside test-dependency names.
evidence: docs/user-guide/accounting.md:586 - '`random_allocation` and `k_out_of_t`, use deterministic transforms.'
Executed: `import opaque.dpsgd.accounting as a; a.__all__` -> ['adaclip', 'gaussian', 'k_out_of_t', 'parallel_poisson', 'poisson'].

git show --stat fc44ec8d lists the deletion of packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_random_allocation.py (216 lines) and .../dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py (225 lines).

A repo-wide grep for `random_allocation` outside .git/.venv finds only this docs line plus internal names that legitimately survive (`_random_allocation_cache`, the native `random_allocation_gaussian_pld`, and the third-party `random_allocation` cross-validation package in tests/accounting/test_cross_validation_allocation.py).
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `random_allocation` with `k_out_of_t` in that sentence (it is already listed), i.e. 'Balls-in-Bins with identity_strategy() and k_out_of_t use deterministic transforms.'
